Wetland census finds new migratory visitors

The annual wetland bird census in north Bihar has recorded three migratory species never documented in the state, raising the tally of waterbird species at the surveyed sites to 112.

Ornithologists said delayed monsoon withdrawal and fuller wetlands likely drew the vagrants, spotted at Kusheshwarsthan and Gogabil.

The census, conducted by the forest department with volunteer birders, covered 14 wetlands over two weekends.

Experts recommended notifying the most productive sites as conservation reserves to shield them from drainage and encroachment.

A detailed report will be submitted to the state wildlife board next month, officials said.
